question: If a client fires off several requests on the same connection without waiting for the earlier responses, does the server work on them concurrently or hold off until each one finishes in order?
answer: Uvicorn supports pipelining pragmatically: it queues up any pipelined HTTP requests and pauses reading from the underlying transport, and it will not start processing a pipelined request until the response for the previous one has been dealt with.

question: If I set a context variable while handling the startup event, will I be able to read that value later inside my request handlers?

question: If my handler sends its response before fully reading the incoming request body, what happens when something later tries to keep reading that body?
answer: Once the response has been sent, Uvicorn stops buffering any further request body data; any subsequent attempt to read the request body will simply get an http.disconnect message instead. This, combined with read flow control, keeps responses that don't read the full request body from accumulating large amounts of unread data in memory.
evidence: Once a response has been sent, Uvicorn will no longer buffer any remaining request body. Any later calls to `receive` will return an `http.disconnect` message.
